aiReview.summary: Agent skill that checklists Flutter macOS toolchain setup (Xcode, CocoaPods, flutter doctor). Not a Mac-native app; listing quality depends on an unverified GitHub skill path.
evidence: Meta description and page body: Xcode installation, CocoaPods, environment validation for Flutter on macOS.
Install: npx skills add https://github.com/flutter/skills --skill flutter-setting-up-on-macos
GitHub tree URL for the skill returned HTTP 404.
Source listing is VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills, not jaywcjlove/awesome-mac.
uncertainty: Whether the Flutter official skills repo still hosts this skill and what SKILL.md actually contains.
Maintenance, license, and whether the skill runs privileged install commands.
aiReview.tagline: Agent checklist for Flutter Xcode and CocoaPods setup
aiReview.description: Guides coding agents through Xcode, CocoaPods, and flutter doctor steps when preparing a Mac for Flutter iOS and macOS builds.
pros: Targets a real Mac-specific Flutter toolchain sequence: Xcode, command-line tools, licenses, and CocoaPods.
States concrete use cases such as flutter doctor Xcode errors and CocoaPods plugin setup.
Published as a community infrastructure skill on officialskills.sh with an install command via npx skills.
cons: This is an agent skill page, not a standalone macOS app or native developer tool.
The linked GitHub skill tree returned 404, so the SKILL.md contents could not be verified.
Similar-skills section on the page is unrelated WordPress and Apollo items, suggesting weak curation.

aiReview.summary: Mac-native Swift CLI that records the main display plus system audio via ScreenCaptureKit without a virtual audio driver. Small MIT repo with limited adoption and a few hard-coded capture limits.
evidence: Repo description and README: sck-record CLI, ScreenCaptureKit, no driver/no sudo, Claude Code skill.
README comparison table vs screencapture, virtual audio drivers, OBS, QuickTime.
Topics include macos, screencapturekit, swift, screen-recording.
About page: 3 stars, 0 forks, MIT license, 11 commits on main.
uncertainty: Cannot verify binary quality, permission UX, or audio/video sync beyond README claims.
Cannot verify commit recency or CI health from the page snapshot.
Sponsor Recall.ai block is marketing, not part of the tool itself.
aiReview.tagline: Headless macOS capture with native system audio
aiReview.description: Record the main Mac display and speaker audio to MP4 via ScreenCaptureKit CLI—no driver, sudo, or mic routing.
pros: Uses Apple ScreenCaptureKit on macOS 13+ so system audio is captured without BlackHole, Loopback, or sudo.
Single Swift source file builds with swiftc and writes H.264/AAC MP4.
MIT-licensed with documented CLI flags, permissions, and limitations.
Includes a Claude Code skill/plugin for agent-driven recording.
cons: GitHub shows only 3 stars, 0 forks, and 11 commits.
Captures the main display only with fixed duration and hardcoded bitrate/codec.
Ctrl-C aborts without finalizing the file.
Not listed in jaywcjlove/awesome-mac; popularity and long-term maintenance are unproven.

aiReview.summary: Mac-native Codex CLI notify-hook setup that plays a completion sound and shows a Notification Center banner via afplay and osascript. Tiny MIT repo (guide plus setup script); useful for Codex-on-Mac users but not a general macOS app.
evidence: GitHub README: copy-pasteable guide for Codex CLI notify hook with sound and macOS notification.
Repo files: setup-codex-notify.sh, codex-notify-macos.md, MIT LICENSE; language Shell.
Stars 4, forks 0, issues 1 as of fetch.
Prereqs stated as macOS and working OpenAI Codex CLI.
uncertainty: Cannot verify script security, notify payload handling, or whether the hook still matches current Codex CLI config.
Maintenance cadence and real-world reliability are not visible from README alone.
aiReview.tagline: Codex CLI completion sound and macOS banners
aiReview.description: Configure OpenAI Codex CLI notify hooks on macOS to play a sound and show a banner via a setup script or manual steps.
pros: Targets macOS specifically using afplay and osascript with the Codex CLI notify hook.
Includes an interactive setup script, config.toml wiring, backup of existing scripts, and a manual troubleshooting guide.
MIT-licensed with a clear uninstall path.
cons: Very small project (few stars, no forks) and depends on Codex CLI already being installed.
Functionality is a short shell hook plus docs, not a maintained desktop app.
README notes payload parsing could be more robust and Linux is out of scope.

aiReview.summary: This candidate is the awesome-mac curated list itself, not a Mac app or tool. The title is a scrape artifact (“HERE”), so it should not be listed as a directory entry.
evidence: canonicalUrl is https://github.com/jaywcjlove/awesome-mac, the same repo used as the directory source.
GitHub description: collecting high-quality macOS software organized by category.
sourceEvidence repeatedly points at README.md with anchorText HERE.
Stars reported on GitHub on the order of 100k+.
uncertainty: Exact current star/fork counts were not verified from the live GitHub API.
Whether the directory policy explicitly forbids listing itself.
aiReview.tagline: Curated catalog of macOS apps organized by category
aiReview.description: Collects macOS software and groups it by category so you can browse and find apps more easily.
pros: The repository is a well-known open curated list of macOS software with a large GitHub following.
It organizes apps by category rather than being a single product.
The project is MIT-licensed and actively maintained as a list, not as an application.
cons: The proposed title is “HERE”, which is broken scrape text rather than a product name.
Listing the parent awesome-mac catalog as an entry is self-referential and does not match Mac app or developer-tool criteria.
It is documentation, not a macOS-native app, SDK, or CLI.

aiReview.summary: Curated open-source list of Swift macOS apps from the awesome-mac maintainer; Mac-native discovery resource, not an app itself.
evidence: GitHub description: curated collection of open-source macOS applications built with Swift.
Discovered repeatedly from jaywcjlove/awesome-mac README.
Topics include macos, swift, swiftui, awesome-list; license CC0-1.0.
uncertainty: Exact last-commit date and freshness of individual app links not verified beyond GitHub page stats.
Quality of every listed third-party app is not audited.
aiReview.tagline: Curated open-source Swift apps for macOS
aiReview.description: Browse a maintained collection of open-source macOS applications written in Swift, with categories and bilingual docs.
pros: Listed in jaywcjlove/awesome-mac and maintained by the same author.
Focuses on open-source macOS apps built with Swift rather than generic web tools.
Public repo with ~1.7k stars, ~150 forks, 1405 commits, CC0-1.0, and English/Chinese READMEs.
cons: It is an awesome-list, so listed apps vary in quality and maintenance.
Does not ship a standalone product or SDK.

aiReview.summary: EmacsWiki’s EmacsForMacOS page is a community index of ports, builds, and setup notes for GNU Emacs on macOS, not a single Mac-native product. Useful as a historical/resource link from awesome-mac, but pages like this often mix stale ports with current advice.
evidence: canonicalUrl is https://www.emacswiki.org/emacs/EmacsForMacOS
sourceEvidence repeatedly cites jaywcjlove/awesome-mac README with anchor text Emacs
type is web_url; proposedRegistryPatch is empty
Fetch of the wiki URL failed with HTTP 402
uncertainty: Current wiki page contents, last-edit date, and which ports are still recommended
Whether awesome-mac intended this wiki vs. a specific Emacs.app (e.g. official GNU NS build)
aiReview.tagline: Community wiki of Emacs ports and Mac setup notes
aiReview.description: Collects Mac Emacs distributions, build options, and community notes for installing and running GNU Emacs on macOS.
pros: Listed in jaywcjlove/awesome-mac as the Emacs entry.
Focuses on macOS-specific Emacs ports and installation paths rather than a generic web app.
GNU Emacs itself is a long-lived, well-known editor with Mac GUI ports (e.g. NS/Cocoa).
cons: The candidate URL is a wiki hub, not a maintained app, SDK, or official download site.
Wiki content is crowd-edited and commonly includes outdated Mac ports and OS versions.
Live page content could not be fetched (HTTP 402), so current accuracy is unverified.

aiReview.summary: Native macOS PDF inspection app (App Store) covering structure, security, JS, metadata, and forensics with local processing. Freemium Pro upsell; Apple silicon and macOS 12+ only.
evidence: Redirects to pdfauditor.app; App Store id 6738956506 with mt=12 (Mac).
FAQ states macOS 12 Monterey+, Apple silicon, local processing, free tier plus Pro pricing.
Marketing and screenshots describe forensic/JS/security inspection rather than a generic PDF editor.
uncertainty: Actual App Store ratings, version history, and Intel compatibility claims beyond the FAQ.
Depth of the free tier versus Pro feature gates.
Whether pura-vida.in vs pdfauditor.app ownership/history is fully documented.
aiReview.tagline: Local macOS PDF forensics, security, and structure inspectio
aiReview.description: Inspect PDF structure, security, JavaScript, metadata, and hidden content locally on Mac without editing files.
pros: Listed in jaywcjlove/awesome-mac and ships as a Mac App Store native app.
Processes files locally and documents inspection-only (non-editing) behavior.
Documents concrete inspection areas: security, JS, forensics, forms, signatures, accessibility, and size analysis.
cons: Requires macOS 12+ and Apple silicon only, so Intel Macs are excluded.
Core advanced features sit behind Pro ($19.99/year or $59.99 lifetime).
Maintenance, update cadence, and independent reviews are not verified from the listing page.

aiReview.summary: MIT-licensed Electron/Next.js desktop client for App Store Connect with local SQLite, Keychain-backed credentials, and optional Docker/MCP. Useful Mac-native listing from awesome-mac; still a small project with credential-handling risk.
evidence: README: Better App Store Connect; macOS 11+ Electron 40 / Next.js 16; MIT; Keychain encryption.
Repo language TypeScript, electron/, forge.config.ts, entitlements.plist, public/icon.icns.
awesome-mac curated_readme sourceEvidence targeting this GitHub URL.
Stars 128, forks 15, issues 9; CI and docker workflows present.
uncertainty: Live download counts, auto-update reliability, and current notarization status not verified beyond README badges.
Security of ASC credential handling not independently audited.
Maintenance cadence beyond file presence not checked against recent commits.
aiReview.tagline: Local App Store Connect desktop client for Mac
aiReview.description: Edit listings, TestFlight, analytics, and reviews locally with encrypted credentials. Optional Docker dashboard and MCP for coding tools.
pros: Listed in jaywcjlove/awesome-mac and ships a signed, notarized macOS 11+ DMG.
MIT-licensed TypeScript app with CI, docs, screenshots, and Docker self-host option.
Local SQLite plus AES-256-GCM credentials stored via macOS Keychain; no telemetry claimed.
Covers ASC workflows including metadata, TestFlight, analytics, reviews, screenshots, nominations, and an optional MCP server.
cons: Electron/Next stack rather than a fully native Cocoa app.
Modest GitHub traction (about 128 stars) relative to the feature surface.
Docker deployment documents no built-in auth, so exposing it needs extra protection.

aiReview.summary: Native Swift/SwiftUI macOS utility for browsing, generating, and editing local SSH keys and config; listed on awesome-mac, but GitHub builds are unsigned/not notarized and the app touches private keys.
evidence: Repo README: native macOS SSH key/config manager, Swift, MIT, features listed.
GitHub metadata: Swift, MIT, 252 stars, 10 forks.
Source evidence: jaywcjlove/awesome-mac README link.
Unsigned/not notarized warning and xattr quarantine workaround in README.
uncertainty: Actual last-commit recency and release cadence not fetched as timestamps.
No independent audit of private-key handling or config-write safety.
App Store availability not claimed or verified.
aiReview.tagline: Native Mac app for SSH keys and config files
aiReview.description: Browse, generate, and organize local SSH keys and Host config entries with a SwiftUI Mac UI, menu bar copy, and optional read-only mode.
pros: Native Swift/SwiftUI macOS app with menu bar extra, not a web wrapper.
Manages ~/.ssh (or a custom workspace), key generation/rename, and SSH config Host editing.
Includes read-only mode to block mutating SSH files.
MIT-licensed source with Makefile/Xcode release packaging; ~252 GitHub stars.
Appears in jaywcjlove/awesome-mac.
cons: Release DMGs are unsigned and not notarized; users must clear quarantine.
README states significant AI-assisted development.
Low fork/issue volume; maintenance and security review of key-handling code are not independently verified.

aiReview.summary: Deprecated experimental React Native fork for Cocoa macOS apps; the repo itself points people to Microsoft’s React Native for Windows/macOS and Catalyst instead of continued use of this codebase.
evidence: README deprecation header: no longer maintained; links microsoft.github.io/react-native-windows and Catalyst discussion.
Repo description: deprecated experimental fork for writing desktop apps using Cocoa.
GitHub metadata: MIT, JavaScript, 11185 stars, 76 open issues.
awesome-mac sourceEvidence anchors as “React Native macOS” to this URL.
uncertainty: Last commit date and whether issues/PRs are still triaged were not independently dated beyond the deprecation notice.
Whether awesome-mac still intends this URL versus microsoft/react-native-macos is unknown.
aiReview.tagline: Deprecated Cocoa fork for React Native desktop apps
aiReview.description: Build macOS apps with a React Native iOS fork via Cocoa. Unmaintained; successors exist elsewhere.
pros: Historically a Mac-native Cocoa fork of React Native with substantial GitHub attention (~11k stars).
MIT-licensed source and CLI-based init/run-macos workflow are documented in the README.
Listed under React Native macOS in jaywcjlove/awesome-mac.
cons: README states the project is no longer maintained and is deprecated in favor of other stacks.
Canonical URL github.com/ptmt/react-native-desktop redirects to ptmt/react-native-macos, not an active successor.
Getting-started notes require Node 4.x and OS X 10.11+, which are obsolete.
The author disclaims the fork as experimental and advises proceeding at your own risk.

aiReview.summary: Native Swift macOS IME for Zhuyin and Pinyin, already listed on awesome-mac; GitHub may lag Gitee as the canonical source.
evidence: awesome-mac sourceEvidence repeatedly points at github.com/vchewing/vchewing-macos.
GitHub description: 唯音輸入法 macOS 版, Swift, 645 stars, InputMethodKit-oriented README.
README: native 注音/拼音 IME, Sandbox, macOS 12+, product site vchewing.github.io, Gitee releases.
uncertainty: Exact last GitHub commit recency versus Gitee was not independently dated.
Notarization/App Store distribution status was not verified.
Issue/security posture beyond README claims was not audited.
aiReview.tagline: Native macOS Zhuyin/Pinyin IME in Swift
aiReview.description: Build or install a sandboxed macOS input method for Traditional and Simplified Chinese with Zhuyin, Pinyin, and custom lexicons.
pros: Listed in jaywcjlove/awesome-mac and is a Swift InputMethodKit app for macOS, not a web wrapper.
README documents Zhuyin and Pinyin modes, separate Simplified/Traditional lexicons, and Sandbox constraints.
Repository includes Makefile/CI, Package.swift, and MulanPSL-2.0 licensing notes.
Runtime target is macOS 12+ with a documented legacy Aqua build for older systems.
cons: README states Gitee holds the latest code and releases, so GitHub can be stale.
Build requires very new Swift/Xcode toolchains, which raises the bar for contributors.
License metadata on GitHub is “Other”; engines use mixed MulanPSL and LGPL terms.

aiReview.summary: Native SwiftUI macOS cleaner and uninstaller (Apple Silicon, macOS 26+) with local scanning, Trash-based uninstall/duplicates, and GPLv3 plus Commons Clause. Fits a Mac tools directory; Intel and older macOS users are excluded.
evidence: GitHub AlexTkDev/MacOSCleaner: Swift, 122 stars, 7 forks, license Other (GPLv3 + Commons Clause).
README: macOS 26+, Apple Silicon only; Smart Cleanup, Forensic Uninstaller, Duplicate Finder, Disk Analyzer, Siri/App Intents.
Discovered repeatedly from jaywcjlove/awesome-mac README as MacOSCleaner.
Substantial SwiftUI source tree under MacOSCleaner/ with cleanup, uninstaller, and App Intents modules.
uncertainty: Notarization/Gatekeeper status of official DMGs versus local builds.
Accuracy and safety of cleanup path catalogs in real-world use.
Issue tracker activity (API reported 0 issues) versus actual bug volume.
aiReview.tagline: Native SwiftUI disk cleaner and app uninstaller
aiReview.description: Scan caches, developer junk, duplicates, and leftovers locally on Apple Silicon, then review before deleting or trashing remnants.
pros: Native Swift 6/SwiftUI app with features such as cleanup, forensic uninstaller, duplicates, disk analyzer, processes, and App Intents.
Listed in jaywcjlove/awesome-mac and ships GitHub Releases plus a documented Swift codebase.
README describes no telemetry, path blocklists, Trash for uninstall/duplicates, and on-device FoundationModels explanations.
Recent versioning (v2.3.0) with wiki, issue templates, and CI workflow files.
cons: Requires macOS 26.0+ and Apple Silicon only; Intel Macs are unsupported.
License is GPLv3 plus Commons Clause, so commercial reuse is restricted despite source availability.
First-run notes include stripping quarantine via xattr for unnotarized/local builds.
Star/fork counts are still modest relative to established cleaners.

aiReview.summary: Mac-native website/app blocker from jaywcjlove/awesome-mac; useful for focus work, but App Store shows no ratings and access is paid after a 7-day trial.
evidence: iTunes lookup id 6476942786: trackName Focus Firewall, kind mac-software, artist Terran.
releaseDate 2024-05-29, currentVersionReleaseDate 2026-10-07, version 1.2.9.
userRatingCount 0; formattedPrice Free with in-app subscription/lifetime in description.
sellerUrl https://focusfirewall.com; primaryGenre Productivity.
uncertainty: Cannot verify real-world blocking effectiveness or energy use claims.
Cannot verify review quality or refund/support experience.
awesome-mac README context around the link was empty in sourceEvidence.
aiReview.tagline: Schedule-based site and app blocking on Mac
aiReview.description: Blocks distracting sites and apps on a work schedule, with pause friction, local reports, and no browser extensions.
pros: Listed as Mac software (kind mac-software) requiring macOS 14+.
App Store listing was updated on 2026-10-07 (version 1.2.9).
Blocks sites without extensions across many browsers and keeps browsing reports on-device.
Source is jaywcjlove/awesome-mac rather than a generic web badge.
cons: App Store reports zero user ratings for the current version.
Full use requires a subscription or lifetime purchase after a 7-day trial.
Vendor notes possible incompatibility with VPNs and enterprise MDM.
Candidate metadata was only an App Store URL with no README facts.

aiReview.summary: Native macOS window switcher that lists every window (not just apps) with previews; open-source core plus optional Pro features. Strong fit for an awesome-mac directory.
evidence: Canonical site https://alt-tab.app/ (redirect from alt-tab-macos.netlify.app) describes per-window switching, previews, Spaces badges.
FAQ: free OSS core; Pro adds search/styles/auto-size; 14-day Pro trial.
GitHub link lwouis/alt-tab-macos; GPL-3.0 stated on the homepage.
Discovered repeatedly from jaywcjlove/awesome-mac README.
uncertainty: Exact current GitHub star/release counts not independently verified in this pass.
Pro pricing amounts not captured from /pricing.
Notarization/signing details beyond the site’s claims.
aiReview.description: Switch among every Mac window with live previews, Space badges, and custom shortcuts. Core app is free and open source.
pros: macOS-native window switcher listed in jaywcjlove/awesome-mac.
GPL-3.0 source on GitHub with a long public changelog since 2018.
Claims native Apple silicon and Intel support, macOS 12+, no telemetry.
Core window switching and previews remain free; Pro is optional.
High public traction (site cites millions of downloads and ~16K GitHub stars).
cons: Some advertised features (search, extra styles) are gated behind AltTab Pro.
Requires Accessibility (and similar) permissions typical of window managers.
Marketing site rebrands as AltTab Pro; free vs paid surface is mixed.
